cleared.check: Monad: mined liquidity removals and fee collections against the source. Blocks 124841070 to 125010503, newest first. 277 transactions with a ModifyLiquidity event of liquidityDelta at or below zero were read and 169 were taken: every PoolManager event in the transaction is ModifyLiquidity (or Swap, in multi+swap), no other transaction in the block emitted a PoolManager event for the same pool, the pool key hashes to the pool id, and the hook has no liquidity permission bits. Set aside: 17 pool touched by another transaction in the block; 38 other PoolManager events in the transaction; 42 pool key not found; 11 fees of a position touched after a swap in the same transaction. For each taken transaction Pool.modifyLiquidity and Position.update were rerun on the PoolManager storage of the parent block read with extsload (slot0, fee growth, ticks, position), the predicted pool liquidity, tick words and position words were compared with the storage at the block, and the owed amount per currency was compared with what left the PoolManager in the receipt. PoolManager events were read with eth_getLogs in 100-block windows from rpc3.monad.xyz, rpc1.monad.xyz and rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com, which refuse larger ranges. Native legs were summed from debug_traceTransaction (callTracer) and, independently, from eth_getBalance of the PoolManager at the block and its parent. The trace is a re-execution by the RPC node's interpreter; the balance and the storage are what block production wrote. Of the 108 native legs (92 with a nonzero amount), 69 are alone in their block and all 69 agree with the balance difference; 18 in shared blocks also agree; 21 in shared blocks differ because other transactions moved native value, so those 21 rest on the RPC node's trace alone. The tick bitmap words are not part of the storage comparison.
cleared.result: All 169 transactions match to the unit with no storage difference: 82 single removals, 48 single fee collections, and 39 transactions with several liquidity actions (35 of them with a swap). They hold 114 removal events and 65 zero-delta collections, 134 events with nonzero fees, and 297 currency legs with a payment, 108 of them native. No amount is above or below the source's value, so no difference exceeds the rounding the source allows. Out-of-range removals paid exactly the rounded-down principal, which differs from the rounded-up value in every such case checked (sensitivity.py), so the comparison can tell the two apart.

cleared.check: Source reading of what a removal or fee collection owes: Pool.modifyLiquidity computes fees with the position's liquidity before the update and FullMath.mulDiv by 2^128 of the wrapped difference of fee growth inside (src/libraries/Position.sol:84-100), principal by SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta and getAmount1Delta with roundUp false for a negative delta (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:261-288) at the slot0 price, which modifyLiquidity does not move (src/libraries/Pool.sol:206-235), and PoolManager.modifyLiquidity credits principal plus fees to the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:158-183). Tick feeGrowthOutside is set on initialisation only when tick <= slot0 tick (src/libraries/Pool.sol:533-538), and cleared ticks are deleted after the fee read (src/libraries/Pool.sol:196-203).
cleared.result: The transcription in analyze2.py follows these lines, and the storage written by block production after each checked transaction equals the transcription's prediction on all five networks, which checks the arithmetic of getFeeGrowthInside, updateTick, Position.update and the pool liquidity update as block production ran them.

leads.question: Monad: 42 transactions were set aside because their pools are not registered in the PositionManager and a 100-block log range rules out reading Initialize events back to deployment. Does an explorer or an archive endpoint with wider log ranges give those pool keys, and do those removals match?
leads.why: Pools created outside the PositionManager are the ones a checker of this kind sees least.

leads.question: Tempo: 1,344 of the 1,366 checked removal and collection events sit in multi-action transactions of one account and are checked only by the net per currency, and only 74 events carried nonzero fees. Do fee-bearing removals of other accounts in older blocks match per removal?
leads.why: A per-removal error could in principle be hidden by an opposite error in the same transaction's add, and the fee path is thinly sampled on Tempo.

leadResults.answer: 1,493 mined transactions with liquidity removals or fee collections on Monad (169), MegaETH (413), Tempo (428), Arc (427) and HyperEVM (56, the whole history) were rerun from the parent block storage. All pay exactly the source's principal plus fees per currency, to the unit, and the storage they left equals the transcription. They contain 1,778 removal events and 681 zero-delta collections, 878 events with nonzero fees and 594 native legs. Native legs were checked from producer-written data: PoolManager balance at block and parent on MegaETH, HyperEVM and Monad (where alone in the block), and the system emitter Transfer logs on Arc. 202 transactions were set aside, with the reasons per network in cleared. No removal paid more than the source formula.
